title: Keep the bank lookups off the common pool

blocks.text: At the end of the day, the payment service reconciles: it asks the bank for the status of every payment of the day. Each lookup blocks until the bank answers, which can take seconds. Last week someone made the lookups parallel, and since then the card authorisations that the same service answers time out for as long as the reconciliation runs. The authorisations use parallel streams and `CompletableFuture`'s async methods without an executor.

items: up to `lookupsAtOnce` lookups wait on the bank at the same time, on threads that belong to the report, and the statuses come back in the order of the ids;
when the report returns, or fails, the threads it used end;
a lookup that fails with an unchecked exception makes `statuses` throw an exception of the same type.

blocks.text: The tests use a bank that answers only when several lookups are waiting on it, and one that fails for a single payment.

cases.says: the report returns one status per payment, in the order of the ids
no lookup runs on a thread of the common ForkJoinPool
as many lookups as the report is allowed wait on the bank at the same time
a lookup's unchecked exception reaches the caller with its own type
the threads that ran the lookups end even when a lookup fails

origin.section: Running the Stream Inside Your Own ForkJoinPool Works, but No Document Promises It

concepts: A parallel stream started inside a task of your own ForkJoinPool runs in that pool, an undocumented JDK behaviour; another kind of executor does not count, and the pool must be shut down and its failures unwrapped from ExecutionException.
